st: Soak the dried hominy and beans together in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain and rinse.
Put them in a large heavy pot with [[12 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered until the hominy begins to soften.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the pork cubes on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic to the skillet and cook for [[3 minutes]], then scrape everything into the pot.
Add the sausage, [[2 tsp]] salt and a splash of water if the pot looks dry. Simmer partly covered until the pork is tender.
Add the sweet potatoes and the cabbage wedges and press them under the liquid. Cook until the vegetables are tender and the stew is thick.
Taste for salt, remove the bay leaves and serve in deep bowls. Leftovers are fried in a pan with an egg the next day.

ing: steaks or fillets, cut in chunks
st: Season the fish with [[1 tsp]] salt and the lemon juice and set it aside in the refrigerator.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Pour in [[6 cups]] water, add the bay leaf and [[1 tsp]] salt, and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes, sweet potato and plantain. Simmer until they are nearly tender.
Lower in the fish chunks and simmer gently, without stirring hard, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Taste for salt, remove the bay leaf and ladle into bowls with the vegetables and fish.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, mashed sweet potato and softened butter in a bowl. Add [[0.75 cup]] warm water a little at a time and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Heat a splash of oil in a skillet and cook the onion, garlic and chili for [[4 minutes]]. Add the tomatoes and cook until thick and dry.
Stir in the drained tuna and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and cook for 3 minutes. Cool the filling.
Roll the dough out thin and cut rounds about 4 inches wide. Put a spoonful of filling on each round.
Fold over to make half moons and press the edges firmly with a fork to seal well.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Fry in batches until golden and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

ing: kidney or pinto, canned is fine
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the pork on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for [[3 minutes]]. Add the bay leaf, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[4 cups]] water.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender.
Add the beans with their liquid and the remaining [[4 cups]] water, and bring to a boil.
Slowly rain in the cornmeal while whisking so no lumps form. Add [[1 tsp]] salt.
Lower the heat and cook, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until the cornmeal is soft and thick like porridge. Add water if it gets too thick.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] oil, remove the bay leaf and serve hot in bowls.

ing: white or kidney, canned is fine
st: If using canned corn or hominy, drain and rinse it. Rinse the beans too.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until it renders its fat and starts to brown.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil, the onion and garlic, and cook for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Add the corn, beans, bay leaf, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[4 cups]] water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer partly covered, stirring now and then, until the corn is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Mash a few spoonfuls against the pot to thicken the mixture, then simmer 10 more minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Have an 8-inch cake pan and a deeper roasting pan ready.
Melt [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a small heavy saucepan over medium heat without stirring until it becomes a deep amber caramel.
Pour the caramel into the cake pan, tilting it to coat the bottom, and let it harden.
Blend the goat cheese, eggs, [[1 cup]] sugar, milk, cinnamon and lemon zest until perfectly smooth.
Pour the mixture over the caramel in the pan.
Put the pan in the roasting pan and pour hot water around it halfway up. Bake until the center is just set with a slight wobble.
Cool completely, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Run a knife around the edge, place a plate on top and flip to unmold, letting the caramel run down the sides.
